_comment: Template for ~/.factotum/<env>/config.json. `factotum init` writes the real one;
this is here to read. The real file is never versioned.
listen: the bind is LOOPBACK. factotum is reached over HTTPS through
`tailscale serve`, which terminates TLS and proxies to 127.0.0.1 — so nothing on
the tailnet can reach the daemon directly, with curl or otherwise. `interface` is
still accepted for an operator who knows why they want it, but it gives up the
local rescue route below.
publicOrigin: the origin the client is served on, and it is REQUIRED. It must be
canonical and carry no trailing dot — no trailing slash, no upper case, no :443.
`factotum init` composes it from `tailscale status`, which returns the name WITH a
trailing dot, so it strips it. The origin policy compares exact strings: a value
that is off by one character means 403 on everything and two lines that look
identical in `factotum doctor`.
The two accepted origins are publicOrigin and, when the bind is loopback, the bind
itself — which is the way in if `tailscale serve` stops. extraOrigins is an escape
hatch for a proxy that is not tailscale serve. Do not add localhost:5173 here: that
belongs in a dev config only. See docs/networking.md.
modules: a module is OFF unless its block says enabled. Everything else in the block
belongs to that module and is validated by its own schema — a bad value disables that
module with a reason and leaves the rest running.
sessions.sites: directories an agent is allowed to write in. ABSOLUTE, no '..', and
nothing is authorised by being inside one of them — a site is allowed because it is
written here. A write outside its site is denied; reading is never asked about; and
Bash is NOT checked against the boundary. Read docs/running-agents.md first.
sessions.sharedPaths: directories writable from EVERY site, declared once — a notes
vault is the case. A session belongs to one site and a site holds one lock, which is
what lets one agent per project run at the same time; a shared path is how they can
all write one place anyway. NOTHING LOCKS a shared path: two agents can write the
same file there at once. Same form rules as a site path, and it must exist.
sessions.catalog: what you can launch. kind is one of none, command or subagent. An
entry naming something that cannot be invoked is disabled with its reason and the
rest of the catalog keeps working.
